claim: Caching a hot read path in front of a database can reduce tail latency substantially, but only when the working set fits in memory and invalidation is correct.
keywords: latency throughput cache architecture software service api scalability performance
limitations: Benefit disappears under write-heavy or low-locality workloads

claim: Introducing a new service boundary frequently increases end-to-end latency rather than reducing it, because network hops and serialisation dominate the savings.
keywords: architecture microservice service latency fails does work criticism hidden costs software
limitations: Magnitude depends heavily on payload size and call depth

claim: Operational burden of a distributed design (deployment, observability, on-call) is routinely underestimated at design time and often exceeds the implementation cost.
keywords: hidden costs operational burden maintenance software architecture deploy cost

claim: Measuring a baseline before any change is the single most common omission in performance work, and without it an improvement cannot be attributed.
keywords: measured performance comparisons baseline benchmark measurement latency throughput evidence

claim: Algorithmic changes that reduce asymptotic complexity may not improve wall-clock time at realistic input sizes, because constant factors and memory locality dominate.
keywords: algorithm optimiz optimis model speedup inference kernel training state art methods accuracy
limitations: Crossover point is workload specific and must be measured

claim: Reported speedups in algorithm papers frequently fail to reproduce when the baseline is tuned as carefully as the proposed method.
keywords: reproducibility reports published ablations negative results criticism retractions algorithm model benchmark
limitations: General methodological finding, not specific to any one method

claim: A held-out test split evaluated repeatedly during development loses its independence and overstates generalisation.
topic: evaluation methodology held-out test split overfitting
keywords: held-out test split dataset accuracy evaluation task metric evidence quality statistical
applicability_conditions: iterative development against a fixed split
limitations: Degree of degradation depends on the number of evaluations

claim: Differential testing against a reference implementation catches numerical divergence that aggregate accuracy metrics hide.
keywords: numerical equivalence tolerance baseline correctness differential reference implementation algorithm
limitations: Requires the reference to be correct
